stem: Apart from hallucinogens the drug capable of producing bad trips and persistentfl ashbacks is
explanation: A bad trip is the most common adverse eff ect of LSD and related substances. It resembles the acute panic reaction but sometimes can be more severe and occasionally associated with psychotic symptoms. A bad trip ends when the immediate eff ects of the hallucinogen wear off though its course is variable. Cannabis can also cause a bad trip.

stem: Anandamide receptors are associated with
explanation: Cannabis is the most commonly used illegal drug, with only a small minority of cannabis users ever using any other illegal drug. It is available in various forms that contain at least 60 psychoactive cannabinoids, the most important of which is 9-delta-tetrahydrocannibinol (THC). Cannabis usage can vary from infrequent situational use to heavy daily use. There are specifi c cannabinoid receptors in the human brain, and the endogenous agonist at this receptor is called anandamide. The role of the endocannabinoid system is yet to be defi ned. Anandamide (weak ligand) are formed from arachidonic acid - belong to endocannabinoid family. The two types of cannabinoid receptors, central (CB1) and peripheral (CB2), bind tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the active ingredient of marijuana. Anandamide lowers intraocular pressure, decreases activity level, and relieves pain. Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 546

stem: According to the modifi cations of 1971 Misuse of Drugs Act in the UK, which of the following was briefl y classifi ed as a class C drug?
explanation: Class A drugs- Include: Ecstasy, LSD, heroin, cocaine, crack, magic mushrooms (whether prepared or fresh), methyl amphetamine (crystal meth), other amphetamines if prepared for injection Class B drugs- Amphetamines, Methylphenidate (Ritalin), Pholcodine Class C drugs- Tranquilisers (including benzodiazepines, z-drugs and gabapen ti noids), khat, some painkillers, GHB (Gamma-hydroxybutyrate). Ketamine was originally in class C but was upgraded to class B in 2014. Cannabis was originally in class B but was downgraded briefl y to class C between 2004 and 2009.

stem: Mr. X was taken to A&E department following ingestion of a street drug and complained of a sensation of bugs crawling beneath the skin. This could be caused by intoxication with
explanation: Cocaine Intoxication: There is increased energy, increased confi dence, heightened self-esteem, and perceived improvement on mental and physical tasks, euphoria, and diminished need for sleep. With high doses agitation, irritability, impaired judgment, impulsive aggression, some symptoms of mania with associated tachycardia, hypertension, and mydriasis are noted. In some, a sensation of bugs crawling beneath the skin (formication) has been reported when under the infl uence.

stem: A patient presents with amphetamine withdrawal at A&E. Which of the following features is most likely to be present?
explanation: Amphetamine is a stimulant that acts by increasing catecholamine availability at synapses. So intoxication must cause symptoms of sympathetic stimulation such as agitation, high blood pressure, palpitations, dry mouth, diarrhoea, diffi cult micturition, increased sweating, and mydriasis (dilated pupils) In some cases intense paranoid thoughts, hypomania and psychotic features can occur. If withdrawal takes place, the symptoms are those of sympathetic underactivity. Chronic use may lead to loss of appetite and weight loss (hence its abuse by those who want to stay slim!). During amphetamine withdrawal, a 'crash'occurs with anxiety, shakiness, unpleasant mood, fatigue, nightmares with rebound REM sleep, headache, profuse sweating (also seen in intoxication), and insatiable hunger (loss of anorexic eff ect). These symptoms peak in 48 to 96 hours and are resolved in 1 week. Kaplan and Sadock. Synopsis of Psychiatry 9th ed. Page 410

stem: Which one of the following is not a feature of Wernicke's encephalopathy?
explanation: The classical triad of ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and confusion is rarely present in Wernicke's encephalopathy. The syndrome is much more common than is widely believed. A presumptive diagnosis of Wernicke's encephalopathy should, therefore, be made in any patient undergoing detoxifi cation who experiences any of the following signs; Ataxia, Hypothermia and hypotension, Confusion, ophthalmoplegia/ Nystagmus, Memory disturbance and coma/unconsciousness.

stem: Which one among the following is reported as an acute adverse eff ect of MDMA use?
explanation: Acute harmful eff ects of MDMA include "increased sweating, nausea and vomiting, and diminished potency despite increased libido. Deaths have occurred associated with dehydration and hyperthermia (a toxic reaction similar to serotonin syndrome appears to exist. Chronic harmful eff ects include possible neuro-toxicity, hepatotoxicity, and possible chronic cognitive impairment. There is tolerance to its eff ects, but dependence does not occur. Hangover eff ects develop 24-48 hours after ingestion including fatigue, anorexia, and depressed mood (which may be severe)". Excerpt from Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry; 2e:543

stem: A 12-year-old boy presents with dizziness, tremors and nystagmus. The urine drug test is negative for alcohol, opioids and amphetamines. Which of the following drugs must be suspected?
explanation: Inhalants are often used by adolescents. No dependence syndrome described with inhalants; no withdrawals noted as per DSM.Signs of intoxication include "dizziness, nystagmus, incoordination, slurred speech, unsteady gait, lethargy, depressed refl exes, psychomotor retardation, tremor, generalized muscle weakness, blurred vision or diplopia, stupor or coma and euphoria". A recent inhalant user may have rashes around nose and mouth; unusual breath odours; the residue of the inhalant substances on body or clothes; and signs of ocular and oropharyngeal irritation. Retrieved from http://www.aafp.org/afp/2003/0901/p869.html

stem: Which of the following symptoms is least likely in those with MDMA withdrawal?
explanation: MDMA abstinence-associated withdrawal symptoms include fatigue, loss of appetite, depression, anxiety, and trouble concentrating. This happens on the same day or 2days after drug use, the most common mental or mood complaints are diffi culty concentrating, depression, anxiety and fatigue. These symptoms strongly resemble a miniature "crash" that is seen as a withdrawal reaction after the use of stimulants. Insomnia (a delay or postponement of sleep) may be seen during active use or intoxication.

stem: A frequent feature of benzodiazepine withdrawal among the following is
explanation: Insomnia is the most frequent feature of BDZ withdrawal and anxiety is the most prominent.

stem: A 34-year-old man admitted for opioid detoxifi cation has a blood pressure of 96/68 mm Hg. Which of the following is a preferred medication for opioid detoxifi cation?
explanation: Clonidine can cause a drop in BP; though lofexidine belongs to the same class, it has less propensity for this eff ect. The best choice in this situation is buprenorphine that is not provided in the MCQ as an option.

stem: Which one among the following is a classic synthetic hallucinogen?
explanation: Classic synthetic hallucinogen LSD wasfi rst synthesized in 1938 by Albert Hoff man from the ergot alkaloids. The compound is also noted in rye fungus that contributed to lethal outbreaks of St. Anthony'sfi re'in the Middle Ages. The compounds are also present in morning glory seeds in low concentrations.

stem: Mrs. X has a history of opioid dependence and is still taking it. She is pregnant now and is willing to consider opioid detoxifi cation. This should be ideally done during
explanation: Women who are pregnant or planning a pregnancy should consider treatment with Methadone. Ideally, the mother should be encouraged to become abstinent prior to delivery-often this may not be possible. If pregnancy begins while a woman is taking high doses of methadone, the dosage should be reduced slowly (e.g., 1 mg every three days), and foetal monitoring must be carried out closely.If considering detoxifi cation, this should be done in the middle trimester - avoid fi rst trimester for the fear of abortion and last trimester for the fear of premature birth.

stem: The lifetime prevalence of dysthymia is
explanation: The lifetime prevalence of dysthymia is 2.5-5% worldwide (Warraich and colleagues 2004). The male: female ratio is 1:2

stem: Which of the following SSRIs has an active metabolite?
explanation: Sertraline also has an active metabolite, N-desmethyl sertraline, which is ten times less potent than sertraline itself. Fluoxetine also has an active metabolite norfl uoxetine with a long half-life.

stem: Which of the following suggests life-threatening symptom of serotonergic syndrome?
explanation: Severe serotonin syndrome can be life-threatening. Signs and symptoms include high fever, seizures, irregular heartbeat or unconsciousness

stem: A 28-year-old man is taking clozapine for the last eight months but still has some interfering positive symptoms despite good concordance and optimum plasma levels. What is the best-proven strategy to augment this treatment?
explanation: Clozapine augmentation has become common practice because an inadequate response to clozapine alone is a frequent clinical event. Clozapine augmentation with Amisulpride has some evidence that suggests this approach may be worthwhile. It may also allow a dose reduction in clozapine for those who have a dose-dependent intolerance. (Ref: The Maudsley prescribing guidelines in psychiatry- 11th edition- 67)

stem: A 33-year-old man who is taking clozapine for the last 15 days presents with unspecifi c clinical symptoms such as fever and tachycardia. After carrying out some blood tests and reviewing the results, you are suspecting myocarditis. The next best step is to;
options: Monitor cardiac enzymes for next 3 days
Stop clozapine and refer to cardiology
Stop clozapine and send patient to the A&E
Start digoxin after discussing with the GP
correctAnswer: Stop clozapine and refer to cardiology
explanation: Because in rare cases clozapine-induced myocarditis can progress rapidly into cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure, all patients should be monitored closely for at least the initial four weeks of treatment. This should include assessment of clinical status for subjective signs of distress, vital signs each visit, electrocardiogram at baseline, and if risks is suspected then weekly laboratory tests including 3Es: eosinophils, ESR (or CRP) and enzymes (troponin). A diagnosis of myocarditis should be followed by prompt discontinuation of clozapine and medical follow-up (urgently refer to a cardiologist) for supportive treatment. It is not an emergency requiring an approach to the A&E. (Retrieved from http://www.uptodate.com/contents/guidelines-for-prescribing-clozapine-in-schizophrenia)

stem: Which of the following is a risk factor for premature ejaculation?
explanation: SSRIs can cause delayed - not premature - ejaculation.

stem: A 33-year-old lady has repeated episodes of high mood, euphoria and spending spree followed by long periods of low mood, sleep disturbances and suicidal ideas. What is the prevalence of her psychiatric diagnosis?
explanation: The descriptionfi ts with bipolar disorder. Consistently in large epidemiological studies, 1.5% prevalence is quoted for bipolar disorders. It is unclear if there is an elevated estimation of depressive disorders and under-diagnosis of bipolar type 2 disorder in these surveys.

stem: A 40-year-old lady complains of a 5-year history of headache, nausea, vomiting, diffi culty swallowing and unusual pains in her arms and legs. All physical investigations have been normal, and the medical team doubt the presence of an organic pathology. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: Somatization disorder is characterised by multiple, recurrent and frequently changing physical symptoms; most patients have a long and complicated history of involvement with medical services.

stem: A 60-year-old man presents with a persistently low mood, early morning waking and a reduced appetite. His wife reports that he has stopped looking after himself but is still drinking adequate amounts offl uid. She thinks his current presentation is related to the death of the family dog. On further questioning, the man reports odd beliefs and admits to hearing voices. Which of the following would you recommend in this scenario?
explanation: The diagnosis is severe depression with psychotic symptoms as he has both mood and psychotic symptoms. Both antidepressants and antipsychotics should be used in the treatment of psychotic depression as thefi rst line. Emergency ECT is recommended if a patient is not eating and drinking, which is not the case in this scenario.

stem: A patient with the bipolar disorder has become manic. What treatment would you give?
explanation: Among mood stabilisers, both Lithium and sodium valproate are recommended as thefi rst line treatment of mania. If the patient is taking any antidepressant medication, it should be stopped immediately.

stem: What is the threshold of considering a drug teratogenic compared to the spontaneous occurrence of major malformations among live-born neonates?
explanation: The incidence of commonly occurring and clinically identifi able abnormalities recognized at birth among liveborn infants is 2%-4% in most series published. If exposure to a treatment is associated with a rate higher that this, the treatment can be suspected to have a teratogenic potential.

stem: The migrants-to-natives prevalence ratio for schizophrenia is estimated to be
explanation: The incidence of schizophrenia is 3 to 5 times more common in migrants than native population; this becomes 1.8 when considering prevalence rates.(Saha, McGrath et al PLoS Medicine 2004).

stem: Patients suff ering from schizophrenia are often seen to be living in inner cities. This is explained by
explanation: The increased frequency of schizophrenia in lower socio-economic groups, urban dwellers and immigrants may be because deprivation causes schizophrenia – the breeder hypothesis – or because the functional decline associated with schizophrenia drives schizophrenic (and preschizophrenic) individuals to cheaper inner city accommodation – the drifter hypothesis. The drifter hypothesis enjoys wider acceptance and is supported by reports of high rates of schizophrenia in homeless people (Marshall, 1994) and in Afro-Caribbean immigrants to the UK.

stem: The prevalence of mania among relatives of individuals with bipolar disorder, as determined by structured clinical interviews, is
explanation: The kappa agreement between structured and clinical diagnostic techniques for mood disorders is poor, ranging from 0.23 to 0.49 in ESEMED study. In the IOWA Study (a prospective investigation of the hereditary nature of schizophrenia and bipolar disorders) the prevalence of mania among relatives of patients aff ected by bipolar disorders, calculated solely on the basis of diagnostic interviews, was 1.9%; however, when additional sources of information such as clinical records and cross-interviewing of relatives were considered, the rate increased to 5.3%.

stem: The personality disorders associated with highest disability in terms of vocational functioning is
explanation: Seminal work by Skodol et al ((Am J Psychiatry 2002; 159:276-283) showed that obsessive-compulsive personality disorder was associated with the least overall functional impairment among the personality disorders, while borderline PD and schizotypal PD had the highest impairment in baseline occupational functioning.

stem: A 23-year-old manfi nds it hard to delegate his job to others. He is rigid and infl exible in adhering to rules and has had various altercations with co-workers concerning his inability to get rid of oldfi les from his offi ce. What is the prevalence of his diagnosis?
explanation: The most striking features of anankastic personality disorder are included in this description. Along with a lack of adaptability to new situations, patients show a lack of imagination, failing to take advantage of opportunities, inhibiting perfectionism making ordinary work a burden and harbour a guilty preoccupation with wrong doing. 17 to 19 per 1000 is the quoted prevalence.

stem: Which of the following rating scales retain the aspects of a clinical examination during a consultation?
explanation: PSE retains the aspects of a mental state examination

stem: Which is NOT true regarding depression?
options: Ethnic minorities and migrants have consistently high rate of depression
Poverty and unemployment are associated with depression across all cultures
Cognitive schemas in depression vary across the cultures
Selective migration of vulnerable individuals cannot explain the incidence of depression among immigrants
Somatic complaints are more frequent among immigrant depressed patients
correctAnswer: Ethnic minorities and migrants have consistently high rate of depression
explanation: Unlike psychosis, depression does not seem to be consistently high in the ethnic minorities. Dinesh Bhugra and Oyedeji Ayonrinde, "Depression in migrants and ethnic minorities," Adv Psychiatr Treat 10, no. 1 (January 1, 2004): 13-17.

stem: Which of the following personality disorders is often included in the bipolar spectrum?
explanation: The relationship between borderline personality disorder and bipolar disorder has been a controversial topic ever since borderline personality disorder was incorporated into DSM in 1980. Some authors argue for a shared spectrum between the two groups.

stem: A nursing mother treated for her bipolar illness brings her 3 weeks old infant to her paediatrician. The baby is hypotonic, lethargic and not taking feeds. On investigation, the baby has elevated liver functions indicating cholestasis. The most likely off ending agent is
explanation: Carbamazepine is excreted via breast milk and can cause cholestatic hepatitis, transient hepatitic dysfunction (Hyperbilirubinaemia, High concentration of gamma-glutamyl-transferase), and seizure like activity, irritability, high-pitched crying, hyperexcitablity and poor feeding in a breast-fed baby.

stem: A mother with bipolar disorder becomes accidentally pregnant despite using barrier contraception. The child shows developmental delays andfi ngernail hypoplasia. The most likely mood stabilizer that was prescribed to the mother is
explanation: In a series of carbamazepine exposed pregnancies, craniofacial defects (11 percent),fi ngernail hypoplasia (26 percent), and developmental delay (20 percent) were recorded. (Jones et al 1989)

stem: Which antidepressant is most eff ective in pathological emotionalism according to RCT evidence?
explanation: Pathological laughing and crying syndrome is also called as emotional incontinence/emotionalism/pseudobulbar aff ect. This refers to spontaneous unprovoked laughter or crying seen in patients wioth brain damage; it occurs in response to non-specifi c stimuli, in the absence of associated mood change (mood incongruent aff ect) and in the absence of voluntary control of facial expression. The aff ect change is generally transient but distressing due to perceived loss of control. In a study 66% of people with MS and pathological laughing / crying responded to 75 mg of amitriptyline per day. Improvement in symptoms also occur with either amantadine or levodopa administration. Fluoxetine and sertraline have been evaluated in small parallel RCTs with favourable results; citalopram in a cross over RCT showed signifi cant benefi ts and fewer side-eff ects, and is commonly used by clinicians.

stem: Persistent apnoea has been reported in babies with which of the following drugs started during breastfeeding?
explanation: Benzodiazepines: Should not be started during breast feeding and should be encouraged to stop before becoming pregnant. Long acting benzodiazepine can produce lethargy, poor suckling and weight loss. Persistent apnoea has been reported with Clonazepam Low dose of short acting benzodiazepine (Temazepam, oxazepam) are mostly safe. Diazepam and alprazolam should be avoided

stem: The most epileptogenic among the newer antipsychotics is
explanation: Clozapine is very epileptogenic. Among 5% who receive more than 600 mg/day develop seizures.

stem: Mr.X is a 37-year-old gentleman with a long-standing diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia for the last 15 years. He also has a history of deliberate self-harm and 2 episodes of failed serious suicide attempts in the past. Which of the following medications would be more eff ective in reducing suicidal behaviour in this patient?
explanation: Clozapine reduces suicide rate in patients with schizophrenia. The Intercept Study compared Clozapine and Olanzapine in 980 patients over a 2 year period and found that the Clozapine group had substantially fewer suicide attempts and fewer hospitalisations related to suicidality.

stem: A 42-year-old lady with schizophrenia has been tried on Olanzapine and Quetiapine appropriate doses for 8 weeks each with poor eff ect. Your next step is to try:
explanation: Kane et al reported a multicenter clinical where schizophrenia patients who had failed to respond to at least three diff erent neuroleptics underwent a prospective, single-blind trial of rather a high dose of haloperidol for six weeks. Patients whose condition remained unimproved inspite of haloperidol were then randomly assigned, in a double-blind manner, to clozapine (up to 900 mg/d) or chlorpromazine (up to 1800 mg/d) for six weeks. Out of 268 patients, 30% of the clozapine-treated patients were categorized as responders compared with 4% of chlorpromazine-treated patients. This improvement included 'negative' as well as positive symptoms.

stem: The most characteristic symptom of SSRI discontinuation syndrome is
explanation: The abrupt withdrawal of SSRI especially paroxetine or fl uvoxamine (shorter half-life), is associated with dizziness, nausea, headache, depression, anxiety, insomnia, poor concentration,fl u-like symptoms, paresthesias, and migraine-like symptoms. It usually requires at least 6 weeks of treatment before discontinuation and resolves spontaneously in 3 weeks. Those who have signifi cant SSRI intolerance during treatment onset will have more discontinuation reactions. Fluoxetine is the SSRI least likely to cause withdrawal syndrome as its metabolite has t1/2 more than 1 week leading to slow self-tapering in plasma. Fluoxetine in some cases can treat discontinuation syndrome or used to prevent it when stopping an SSRI suddenly. But delayed withdrawal syndrome can occur withfl uoxetine too.

stem: Which of the following may help diff erentiating borderline personality from bipolar disorder?
options: Impulsivity in bipolar disorder is chronic rather than episodic
Mood changes lasts for many days in borderline personality
Emptiness is often used as the mood descriptor in borderline personality
Elated mood shifts are often seen in borderline personality
correctAnswer: Emptiness is often used as the mood descriptor in borderline personality
explanation: In Bipolar Disorder the onset is in early 20s (later than borderline), mood changes are observable spontaneoulsy rather than being precipitated solely by external events, if present, episodic self harm attempts are usually related to depression, though self mutilation is rare. Patients with borderline PD use 'emptiness' as a descriptor for their mood more often than those with bipolar disorder.

stem: A 44-year-old woman repeatedly visits her dentist with numbness around her mouth and pain in the right jaw. There was no observablefi nding on oral and dental examination, and the clinical picture seems inconsistent to the dentist, who refer her to your clinic. The most likely diagnosis is
explanation: The term atypical facial pain wasfi rst introduced by Frazier and Russell in 1924. The pain is atypical in its distribution, unilateral and poorly localised - notfi tting with any cranial neuralgia. It lasts most of the day and is described as a severe ache, crushing or burning sensation. The Headache Classifi cation Subcommittee of the International Headache Society (2004) described persistent idiopathic facial pain (PIFP) as Psychiatric symptoms of depression and anxiety are prevalent in this population. Treatment is very diffi cult and requires a multidisciplinary approach to address the many facets of this pain syndrome. Pain disorder is one of several somatoform disorders described in the revised DSM-IV-TR.

stem: Psychotic illness in multiple sclerosis is most commonly observed in the context of treatment with
explanation: Exogenous steroids can induce both aff ective disturbances and psychosis.

stem: 'Giant Panda sign' is an MRIfi nding characteristic of
explanation: Wilson's disease: MRI may show intense hyperintensity of the midbrain with relative sparing of red nucleus, superior colliculus and part of the pars reticulata of substantia nigra with hypointensity of the aqueduct sometimes called "Giant Panda sign".

stem: 'Real-life test' forms part of the treatment options for which psychiatric condition?
explanation: Real-life test forms part of the treatment options for Transsexualism. Most centres require a successful real-life test of at least one year prior to consideration for surgery. During this time the patient undertakes to live full time and attempt tofi nd employment in the new sex. Patients will change their name and come out to friends and family. Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 758

stem: A 33-year-old man is suspected to have various sexually transmitted illnesses and possibly HIV. He presents with cognitive impairment. Which of the following cells in his brain are least likely to be directly aff ected by HIV?
explanation: Theoretically all the main cell types of the CNS, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, neurons, perivascular macrophage and microglia, can be infected by HIV-1 since they possess the receptors and/or co-receptors for HIV-1 entry, but only the latter two are the most commonly infected cells by HIV-1. Most studies have indicated an absence of in vivo infection in neurons - It is unclear whether detection of infected neurons is complicated by the loss of the infected neuronal populations.

stem: A 34-year-old lady presents with recurrent episodes of binge eating but has no weight control behaviour. She has a general tendency to overeat and looks overweight. Which of the following is correct regarding this presentation?
options: Nearly a quarter of those suff
ering from this problem are males
Her condition will not remit spontaneously
Stressful periods are associated with decline in binges
correctAnswer: Nearly a quarter of those suff ering from this problem are males
explanation: Recurrent episodes of binge eating in the absence of extreme weight-control behaviour generally occurs in a background of a tendency to overeat. This is referred to as Binge Eating Disorder and is associated with obesity. Patients are typically in their 40s with an overrepresentation of males when compared to other eating disorderarly 25% of all binge-eating population are males.

stem: A 34-year-old patient is started on sertraline by her GP. As a part of local monitoring system the GP administers a depression rating scale whose minimal score to diagnose depression is 7. The patient's initial score is 22/62. Her score drops to 11/62 in 8 week's time. Which of the following is true?
options: The patient is in partial response
explanation: Non-response is usually defi ned as 25% or less decrease in symptom severity compared with baseline. Partial response is 26-49% decrease in symptom severity compared with baseline. Response is 50% or greater decrease in severity of symptoms compared with baseline. Remission refers to an absence of symptoms defi ned by absolute scale (for example, score of 7 on Hamilton rating scale for depression).

stem: A 44-year-old patient has been admitted many times with a relapse of bipolar disorder in last few years. To be classifi ed as a rapid cycler, which of the following categories must he satisfy?
options: More than 4 relapses of either mania or depression in the last year
More than 4 episodes requiring hospitalisation in 1 year
More than 4 episodes of switch in a week
More than 4 manic episodes in last 1 year
correctAnswer: More than 4 relapses of either mania or depression in the last year
explanation: The defi nition of rapid cycling is having greater than or equal to 4 episodes/year. This includes both depression and mania. Patients who have at least 4 episodes/month are considered ultra-rapid cyclers and those who switch within a day on at least 4 days/week are termed ultra-ultra rapid or ultradian cyclers.

stem: A 46-year-old man with schizophrenia is admitted with a history of heavy drinking, poor self-hygiene and self-neglect. He is confused, agitated and has visual hallucinations. Which of the following is most important to avoid?
explanation: In patients with alcohol related delirium or cognitive change, start thiamine prior to or concurrently with treatment of intravenous glucose solutions, and continue until the patient resumes a normal diet. The administration of dextrose or other carbohydrates in this setting can be hazardous, because glucose oxidation is a thiamine-intensive process that may drive the last reserves of circulating vitamin B-1 toward the intracellular compartment, thereby aggravating neurologic damage

stem: A 46-year-old lady has been treated with Tamoxifen for breast cancer. She is also clinically depressed and will need treatment with antidepressants. Which one among the following should be avoided due to its eff ects upon Tamoxifen?
explanation: In several studies (notably, Jin et al, 2005), concurrent use of tamoxifen with the potent CYP2D6-inhibitor antidepressants such as duloxetine, bupropion, paroxetine andfl uoxetine, was associated with a signifi cant reduction in circulating endoxifen levels in some women and therefore should be avoided.

stem: A 50-year-old man with a history of paranoid schizophrenia has been prescribed 600 mg of Quetiapine. During a routine screening with ECG, he has a QTc interval of 510 ms. He does not report any cardiac symptoms. The appropriate next step would be
options: Cross taper quetiapine with Olanzapine and repeat ECG in 2 weeks
Repeat ECG in 2 weeks, since patient is asymptomatic
Repeat ECG and refer to cardiology if T wave is abnormal
Reduce the dose of Quetiapine, repeat ECG and consider referral to cardiology
correctAnswer: Reduce the dose of Quetiapine, repeat ECG and consider referral to cardiology
explanation: Strong evidence links QTc values over 500 ms to a clearly increased risk of arrhythmias. The dosage should be reduced immediately and consider referral to a cardiologist immediately.

stem: A 54-year-old woman gives a history suggestive of acute anxiety. Which of the following is not consistent with a diagnosis of panic disorder?
options: Episodes of unconsciousness in a crowded supermarket
Recurrent experience of pressure symptoms on the chest
correctAnswer: Episodes of unconsciousness in a crowded supermarket
explanation: Falling 'unconscious' suggests organic cause.

stem: A 56-year-old lady treated for bipolar depression wants to know which drug can prevent both mania and depression equally well. The best option is
explanation: Bauer et al proposed that an agent be considered a mood stabilizer if it has effi cacy in each of four distinct uses: 1) treatment of acute manic symptoms, 2) treatment of acute depressive symptoms, 3) prevention of manic symptoms, and 4) prevention of depressive symptoms. According to their analysis only lithium was eligible to be called a mood stabiliser.

stem: A Glasgow coma scale between 9-12 indicates which of the following?
explanation: The GCS is scored between 3 and 15, 3 being the worst, and 15 the best. It is composed of three parameters : Best Eye Response, Best Verbal Response, Best Motor Response.A Coma Score of 13 or higher correlates with a mild brain injury, 9 to 12 is a moderate injury and 8 or less a severe brain injury. Teasdale G., Jennett B., LANCET (ii) 81-83, 1974.

stem: An ST1 trainee in psychiatry sustains a needlestick injury despite wearing gloves. The patient is suspected to have HIV. The risk of HIV transmission from seropositive individuals following a needlestick injury in health care workers is about
explanation: The risk of infection of health care workers after a needlestick accident is rare, about 1 in 300. After infection with HIV, AIDS is estimated to develop in 8 to 11 years, although this time is gradually increasing because of early treatment.

stem: A young man in your clinic complains of stiff ness soon after starting antipsychotic treatment. Which of the following scales could most likely measure the severity of acutely developing EPSEs?
explanation: Acute EPSEs such as dystonia, parkinsonism are measured using Simpson Angus scale; tardive dyskinesia can be measured using AIMS scale

stem: Factors associated with increased psychiatric morbidity following head injury would include all except
options: Increased duration of loss of consciousness
Elderly patient with history of alcoholism
explanation: After head injury, patients who are not able to resume previous activities are the ones who had a longer duration of PTA than those who resumed work without problems.

stem: Focused family interventions are particularly useful in which of the following subgroups with eating disorders?
explanation: Family interventions that directly address the eating disorder are especially useful for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa

stem: For a patient suff ering fromfi rst-time relapse of schizophrenia the most eff ective dose of risperidone is
explanation: For risperidone, a dose of 2 mg daily consistently produced a lower level of effi cacy. Doses of 6 mg or greater produced no additional benefi t and doses tend to be less effi cacious at 10 mg daily and above. (Ezewuziie and Taylor, 2006). The optimal dose of risperidone in relapsed schizophrenia is 4mg daily. Higher doses are unlikely to improve effi cacy and may reduce it.

stem: For male to female transsexuals, all of the following surgical procedures are performed except;
explanation: Surgery for male to female transsexual patients involves Orchidectomy and Penectomy with Vaginoplasty using penile skin. The cosmetic results can be good, although candidates vary in their ability to be orgasmic post-surgery. For FTM patients' surgery involves bilateral mastectomy, hysterectomy, and bilateral salpingo-oopherectomy. Phalloplasty is undertaken in less than half of patients as current techniques are neither cosmetically acceptable nor functional for penetration. Ref: Oxford handbook of psychiatry; 759

stem: Four patients are admitted simultaneously with depression. Mrs A is a 36-year-old woman with 2 previous episodes. Mr B is a 33-year-old man with afi rst episode. Mrs C has had one previous episode of depression. Mr D, aged 77, has had at least 6 previous episodes. Which of the following is true?
options: Those who do not have recurrence in next 2 years will be free from depression thereafter.
Mr B will have highest recurrence rate.
At least one of them will have a recurrence in next 6 months.
None of the other listed optiions is true
The recurrence rate will be lowest for Mr D given his age.
correctAnswer: At least one of them will have a recurrence in next 6 months.
explanation: About 25 percent of patients experience a recurrence of major depressive disorder in thefi rst 6 months after release from a hospital, about 30 to 50 percent in the following 2 years, and about 50 to 75 percent in 5 years. Approximately 50% of patients who experience an episode of major depression will have a recurrence within 5 years. For patients who have had two major depressive episodes, the probability of recurrence increases to 70%, and after three episodes it increases to 80% to 95%

stem: Graded exercise therapy is a treatment option recommended for which psychiatric condition?
explanation: Graded exercise therapy is a treatment option recommended for Chronic fatigue syndrome. It is based physiological model of deconditioning. Muscles strength, autonomic response and perception of exercise related sensation are aff ected by inactivity. Therapy aims to gradually increase the exercise and other activities thus reducing the unwanted consequences of inactivity. CBT and graded exercise therapy are the only eff ective treatments for CFS.

stem: In the immediate management of panic disorder which of the following is correct?
options: Dose escalation is an optimum strategy for SSRIs
Combination of CBT and SSRIs must be tried whenever possible
Benzodiazepines must be given for all those waiting for CBT
Psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy have comparable effi
correctAnswer: Psychotherapy and pharmacotherapy have comparable effi cacy
explanation: acute management according to patient choice: pharmacological: all SSRIs, some TCAs (clomipramine, imipramine), some benzodiazepines (alprazolam, clonazepam, diazepam, lorazepam), venlafaxine, reboxetine have evidence base. psychological: cognitive-behaviour therapy Both pharmacological and psychological approaches have broadly similar effi cacy in acute treatment. Routinely combining drug and psychological approaches is not recommended

stem: Both CBT and mentalization-based therapy have a positive eff ect in treating depression. A randomised, parallel group, assessor-blinded superiority clinical trial is planned to compare the two approaches. 84 consecutive adult participants diagnosed with major depressive disorder and receiving antidepressant treatment, (unchanged for the last 6 weeks) will be included over the course of 2 years, randomised to either CBT or mentalization-based therapy. The primary outcome is a change in the Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression at cessation of treatment (18 weeks). The investigators intend to use an Intention to Treat Analysis (ITT) when reporting the study results. Excluding which of the following subjects will not aff ect the principle of ITT analysis?
options: Patients in Mentalization arm who disclose receiving private CBT sessions
Patients who disclose a new private prescription offl
Patients who withdraw their consent after completing the trial
Patients who are allocated to CBT halfway after incorrectly receiving treatment in the Mentalization arm.
correctAnswer: Patients who are allocated to CBT halfway after incorrectly receiving treatment in the Mentalization arm.
explanation: Intention to treat approach maintains treatment groups that are similar, apart from random variation. This is the reason for randomisation, and the feature may be lost if the analysis is not performed on the groups produced by the randomisation process. For this reason, dropouts due to death or consent-withdrawal must not be excluded (Note: ethical permission must be sought beforehand to use the data from patients who discontinue the trial). Certain protocol-deviations may also happen in real world practice: e.g. self-medicating patients or those who do not take the treatment as prescribed. These exceptions must not induce exclusion of patients in an ITT analysis. Excluding randomised patients from the primary analysis may be legitimate when study personnel made errors in the implementation of eligibility criteria or when patients did not receive the correct intervention – an error that can happen only in a trial set-up. Ref: Fergusson et al BMJ. 2002; 325(7365): 652 –654 & Hollis & Campbell, BMJ 1999;319:670

stem: A randomized trial of oral antiretroviral therapy was conducted to evaluate the use of antiretroviral treatment as preexposure prophylaxis among HIV-1 –serodiscordant heterosexual couples from Kenya and Uganda. The HIV-1 –seronegative partner in each couple, was randomly assigned to one of the three study regimens — once-daily tenofovir (TDF), combination tenofovir – emtricitabine (TDF –FTC), or matching placebo — and followed monthly for up to 36 months. Of the enrolled 4758 couples 4747 were followed: 1584 randomly assigned to TDF, 1579 to TDF –FTC, and 1584 to placebo. A total of 82 HIV-1 infections occurred in seronegative participants during the study, 17 in the TDF group, 13 in the TDF –FTC group and 52 in the placebo group, indicating a relative reduction of 67% in the incidence of HIV-1 with TDF (95% confi dence interval [CI], 44 to 81; P<0.001) and of 75% with TDF –FTC (95% CI, 55 to 87; P<0.001). Protective eff ects of TDF –FTC and TDF alone against HIV-1 were not signifi cantly diff erent (P=0.23), and both study medications signifi cantly reduced the HIV-1 incidence among both men and women. Eight participants receiving active treatment were found to have been infected with HIV-1 at baseline, and among these, antiretroviral resistance developed in two during the study. An estimate of the primary endpoint in the modifi ed Intention-to-Treat Analysis is shown in a graph below. The primary endpoint of this study is
options: Antiretroviral treatment response in seropositive partners
Emergence of immunity against HIV-1 infection
explanation: This study evaluated the ability of antiretroviral treatment to prevent HIV-1 infection in individuals who have seropositive partners. The preexposure prophylaxis was provided to originally seronegative partners.

stem: As a specialty doctor in an addiction clinic, you are concerned that the increase in the rate of sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) in your area may be linked to high rates of methamphetamine use locally. You conduct a qualitative study initially by interviewing several patients and devise an educational intervention (FATA: Focussed Addiction Therapist Advice). To test the eff ectiveness of this intervention, you decided to provide FATA to alternate patients attending your clinic. Using this information answer the following question. To test your hunch that FATA is an eff ective intervention, what study design have you used in the above scenario?
explanation: You are testing an intervention – i.e. conducting a trial. You have some 'controls' for whom the active treatment is not being off ered (i.e. your alternate patients who don't receive FATA). So you are running a controlled trial. You haven't randomised this sample, so this is a simple controlled trial, but not randomised. Note that the non-randomised controlled trials can detect associations between an intervention and an outcome, though they cannot rule out the possibility that the association was confounded.

stem: For healthcare interventions not restricted to a specifi c specialty, which database is commonly used to identify observational studies?
explanation: For healthcare interventions, MEDLINE and Embase are the databases most commonly used to identify studies of all types. stem: Heterogeneity in a systematic review can be identifi ed using statistical tests such as
explanation: Heterogeneity can be identifi ed using statistical tests such as chi-square or the analysis of variance (ANOVA). It is usually identifi ed prior to a meta-analysis calculation. Chi-square tests of heterogeneity can be either Q test or I test.

correctAnswer: Selecting subjects who are uniform for confounding variables
explanation: The best method is to avoid confounders by sampling in a matched fashion. But one may not be able to avoid unknown confounders in this manner.

stem: If the sensitivity of a test increases which of the following occurs?
options: The power of statistical test drops.
The false positive error rate increases.
The false negative error rate increases.
correctAnswer: The false positive error rate increases.
explanation: When sensitivity increases, more number of cases will be diagnosed despite not having the disease (an increase in false positive rate). When you select a lower criterion value, then the true positive fraction and sensitivity will increase. On the other hand, the false positive fraction will also increase, and, therefore, the true negative fraction and specifi city will decrease.

stem: In a forest plot, what does the horizontal line passing through the block depict?
explanation: In a forest plot, the horizontal line passing through the block depicts the confi dence interval. In other words, the lines running across the 'OR' (Odds ratio) dot represents the confi dence interval for that odds ratio.

stem: In a sample of 300 volunteers, IQ is measured and the value is plotted as a distribution curve across the sample. It is found that the mean, median, and mode are all the same for the sample studied. Which of the following statistical distribution refers to the above pattern?
explanation: One of the characteristic features of Normal or Gaussian distribution is that the mean, median and mode of the observations lie at the same point. A bimodal distribution has 2 mode values. In a negatively skewed distribution, the mean is lesser than the median. The tail of such a distribution is longer on the left than the right (negative outliers). In a positively skewed distribution, the mean is greater than the median. The tail of such a distribution is longer on the right than the left (positive outliers).

stem: In a scale designed to measure the creativity of a population, it was found that the scores obtained were normally distributed. If mean score is 10 and standard deviation is 1, then the proportion of population who will score between 9 and 11 is
explanation: The value 9 is nothing but (mean – 1SD) while 11 is (mean + 1SD). Between -1 and +1SD we can expect to see 68% observations in a normal distribution.

stem: In a study comparing two treatments for depression, which of the following is associated with greater statistical power?
options: Comparison of active drug against active drug
The use of a categorical outcome variable
Comparison of active drug against placebo
correctAnswer: Comparison of active drug against placebo
explanation: When two active compounds are compared, the observed size of the eff ect tends to be smaller for a given sample size. But when a placebo is compared against an active drug, the power of a study increases.

stem: In a systematic review of studies looking at Duration of Untreated Psychosis and outcome, two types of study designs are noted. One group of studies categorically divided DUP to binary variable long DUP and short DUP and assessed the outcome. Another group of studies correlated the duration of DUP with the severity of the outcome. Which of the following best describes the above phenomenon?
explanation: In systematic reviews, heterogeneity refers to variability or diff erences between studies in the estimates of eff ects. A distinction should made between "statistical heterogeneity" (diff erences in the reported eff ects), "methodological heterogeneity" (diff erences in study design) and "clinical heterogeneity" (diff erences between studies in key characteristics of the participants, interventions or outcome measures). In this question, the study methods are diff erent – as a result methodological heterogeneity has resulted. (from Bandolier)

stem: The absolute diff erence between two treatments in a study is 10% (95% C.I; 5% to 15%). What is the 95% C.I for the NNT.
explanation: 95% C.I for NNT is calculated by using the 95% C.I values of the ABI (Absolute diff erence). The NNT for the ABI of 5 is 1/0.05=20. The NNT for the ABI of 15 is 1/0.15=6.6, corrected to 7. So, the C. I for the NNT is 7 to 20.

stem: The medical database where you can obtain papers related to nursing and allied health disciplines is
explanation: CINAHL (Cumulative Index of Nursing and Allied Health) indexes journals in thefi elds of nursing and allied health from 1982. PsycINFO is an abstract database of psychological literature from the 1800s to the present. EMBASE (Excerpta Medica database) is a biomedical database that contains bibliographic records with citations, abstracts and indexing derived from biomedical articles in peer-reviewed journals, and is especially strong in its coverage of drug and pharmaceutical research from 1974. stem: The most conservative way of dealing with missing data in intention to treat analysis is
explanation: In the worst case scenario analysis, all missing data is treated as non-responders for the intervention group and responders for a control group (the worst possible case for the researcher). This is the most conservative of all methods tofi ll missing data.

stem: The most frequently combined studies in meta-analyses are
explanation: RCTs are the most frequently combined studies for a meta-analysis though it is possible to combine other study designs.

stem: Which of the following bias is controlled by allocation concealment?
explanation: Allocation concealment helps to reduce selection bias while blinding helps to reduce ascertainment bias.

stem: Which of the following clinical questions is better suited to qualitative rather than quantitative research methods?

stem: Which of the following conditions must be satisfi ed for odds ratio to come close or be the same as a relative risk?

correctAnswer: The prevalence of the disease is very low
explanation: In case of disorders that have a low prevalence, odds ratio comes closer to relative risk.

stem: Which of the following data can provide a link between exposure to a risk factor and the disease studied?
explanation: Incidence rates are useful in epidemiological research for causality. Incidence rates can provide data on new cases developing after an exposure within a time period in a specifi ed population. Thus they are more useful than prevalence data to obtain a link between exposure and disease development.

stem: Bias For each of the questions below, chose one bias from the given list: Intention to treat analysis aims to eliminate this bias Blinding reduces this bias Cohort studies are especially prone to this bias Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: Intention to treat analysis aims to eliminate this bias → Attrition bias, Blinding reduces this bias → Measurement bias, Cohort studies are especially prone to this bias → Attrition bias
explanation: Explanations: Dropouts are included in thefi nal analysis when ITT principle is employed. Measurement bias is reduced by proper blinding in a trial. Recall bias is more common in case-control designs.

stem: Consensus statements for research studies For each of the descriptions below choose one appropriate proposal or guideline regulating the report or conduct of research studies Minimum set of items for reporting in systematic reviews and meta-analyses A structured approach whereby research ethics committees review proposals for RCTs Proposal to improve the reporting of observational studies in thefi eld of epidemiology Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: Minimum set of items for reporting in systematic reviews and meta-analyses → PRISMA, A structured approach whereby research ethics committees review proposals for RCTs → ASSERT, Proposal to improve the reporting of observational studies in thefi eld of epidemiology → STROBE
explanation: Explanation: PRISMA - Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses - is an evidence-based minimum set of items for reporting in systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Though the main focus is on RCTs, PRISMA can also be used as a basis for reporting systematic reviews of other types of research. Meta-analysis Of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) group suggested a proposal for reporting a meta-analysis of observational studies in epidemiology ('MOOSE'). STROBE stands for an international, collaborative initiative of epidemiologists, methodologists, statisticians, researchers and journal editors involved in the conduct and dissemination of observational studies, with the common aim of STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology. The ASSERT statement is the articulation of A Standard for the Scientifi c and Ethical Review of Trials. It proposes a structured approach whereby research ethics committees review proposals for and monitor the conduct of, randomized controlled clinical trials. CONSORT statement is an evidence- based, minimum set of recommendations for reporting RCTs. QUOROM statement is an evidence-based minimum set of recommendations for improving the quality of reporting of meta-analyses of clinical randomised controlled trials (RCTs).

stem: Searching PubMed Database Select the one most appropriate term to be used when searching for published articles using PubMed MEDLINE Index that best matches with each of the following statements: The operator term used to retrieve citations which includes all the search terms A research student would like to expand a search to include all those terms with a speci f ic text The default operator term used in Pubmed The operator term which includes all studies that contain term C, or term C, or both C and D. Choose... Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: The operator term used to retrieve citations which includes all the search terms → AND, A research student would like to expand a search to include all those terms with a speci f ic text → Asterisk (*), The default operator term used in Pubmed → AND, The operator term which includes all studies that contain term C, or term C, or both C and D. → OR
explanation: 1) AND is an operator term used to retrieve citations, which includes all the search terms. It includes only those studies that contain both terms of interest 2) Asterisk (*) can be used to search for all studies containing words beginning with the letters before the asterisk (*) e.g. Depress* will identify all studies with the words 'depression', 'depressive' anywhere in the citation or abstract 3) AND is a default operator term used in PubMed. If you type in two words, in the search box, PubMed would assume that the operator AND has been inserted between the two words. 4) OR- the operator term used to retrieve citations in which each citation includes atleast one of the search terms. It includes all studies that contain term C, or term D, or both C and D.

stem: Epidemiological concepts: For each of the following descriptions choose the appropriate expression from the list above Number of deaths due to a disease expressed as a ratio of number of diseased people. Number of deaths during a calendar year expressed in terms of midperiod population of the area. Number of deaths due to a disease expressed as a ratio of midperiod population of the area. Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: Number of deaths due to a disease expressed as a ratio of number of diseased people. → Case fatality rate, Number of deaths during a calendar year expressed in terms of midperiod population of the area. → Crude mortality rate, Number of deaths due to a disease expressed as a ratio of midperiod population of the area. → Cause specifi c mortality rate
explanation: Explanation: Epidemiologists use specifi c terms for disease occurrence which are commonly tested in the exam. The incidence of a disease is defi ned as the number of new cases of the disease per unit time divided by the population at risk for the disease. The prevalence of a disease is defi ned as the number of individuals with the disease divided by the population at risk for the disease at a specifi c point in time. The crude annual mortality rate is defi ned as the total number of deaths in a population at risk per year divided by the size of the population at risk at mid-year. The population size is measured at mid-year to establish an average size for the population as some patients will die early in the year while others will die late in the year. The crude annual mortality rate is used to measure mortality from all causes over the period of a year. A more specifi c rate is obtained from the cause-specifi c annual mortality rate in which a particular cause of death is of interest. It is defi ned as the number of deaths due to the cause of interest per year divided by the size of the population at risk measured at mid-year. Occasionally, we wish to investigate the death rate due to a particular cause by age; the age-specifi c annual mortality rate is defi ned as the number of deaths in a given age group at risk per year divided by the size of the population at risk measured at mid-year.

stem: Statistical concepts (2) Identify the most appropriate term, which corresponds to the description below The probability that your experiment will f ind a pre-speci f ied difference when one truly exists The spread of the raw data A measure re f lecting the probability of making a false positive conclusion from the results. A measure of the difference between actual and expected frequencies. Choose... Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: The probability that your experiment will f ind a pre-specif ied difference when one truly exists → Power, The spread of the raw data → Standard deviation, A measure re f lecting the probability of making a false positive conclusion from the results. → P-value, A measure of the difference between actual and expected frequencies. → Chi-square statistic
explanation: 1) Power is the ability of a statistical test to detect a difference if such a difference actually exists. It is usually set at 80% 2) Standard deviation is the spread of the raw data and is a measure of the spread of scores away from the mean. 3) P-value is the probability that the result observed in the study is due to chance. A p value less than 0.05 (5%) is often considered to be statistically signi f icant in medical research. P value refers to the chance of type I error (Falsely rejecting a correct null hypothesis) 4) Chi-square test is a test of association between 2 categorical values and the value of Chi-square statistic is a measure of the difference between actual and expected frequencies.

stem: Psychiatry & Endocrine disorders (1) Using the clinical descriptions given below, identify the most probable disorder in the given list. A 35-year-old gentleman presenting with fatigue, muscle pain, depression, and increased thirst. His wife reports an insidious change in personality A 42-year-old woman with paroxysmal palpitations and raised blood pressure. She was referred to psychiatrist for severe anxiety and panic attacks A 56-year-old gentleman presented to GP with a history of polyuria, polydipsia, tiredness and weakness. He tested positive for urinary ketones A 44-year-old woman presented to GP with a history of low mood, lethargy, constipation and menstrual irregularities. Choose... Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: A 35-year-old gentleman presenting with fatigue, muscle pain, depression, and increased thirst. His wife reports an insidious change in personality → Hyperparathyroidism, A 42-year-old woman with paroxysmal palpitations and raised blood pressure. She was referred to psychiatrist for severe anxiety and panic attacks → Pheochromocytoma, A 56-year-old gentleman presented to GP with a history of polyuria, polydipsia, tiredness and weakness. He tested positive for urinary ketones → Diabetes mellitus, A 44-year-old woman presented to GP with a history of low mood, lethargy, constipation and menstrual irregularities. → Hypothyroidism
explanation: 1) Hyperparathyroidism is caused by enlargement of parathyroid glands leading to too much production of parathyroid hormone and increased levels of calcium in the blood. The clinical features include back pain, bone pain, blurred vision, depression, profound change in personality, fatigue, increased thirst, increased urinary output, itchy skin, nausea, loss of appetite and muscle pain. 2) Phaeochromocytoma is characterized by increased heart rate, increased blood pressure, palpitations, and anxiety often resembling a panic attack, along with headaches & diaphoresis. 3) Diabetes mellitus is characterised by polyuria, polydipsia, tiredness, and weight loss, and the presence of urinary ketones. 4) Hypothyroidism is characterised by weight gain, constipation, puff y face, intolerance to cold, menorrhagia, hoarse voice, depression, cognitive diffi culties, dry skin, tiredness & lethargy and bradycardia.

stem: Eponymous syndromes (1) Find one eponym each for each of the syndromes described below: Mr. Yardley is a prisoner awaiting trial and when he was asked 'What is the capital of England, he answered 'Paris'. correctAnswer: Mr. Yardley is a prisoner awaiting trial and when he was asked 'What is the capital of England, he answered 'Paris'. → Ganser's syndrome, A 34-year-old gentleman is convinced that his wife is not his real wife and has been replaced by an imposter who looks just like her. → Capgras syndrome, Mrs. Zakaria is a 30-year-old woman who has recently become pregnant. Her husband has developed morning sickness, abdominal pain, and unusual food cravings after he found out that she was pregnant → Couvade syndrome, A 46-year-old man is convinced that is skin is infested with multiple, tiny mites and insects. → Ekbom's syndrome, A 73-year-old gentleman who has been grossly neglecting himself, hisfl at being untidy andfi lthy, hoards up objects of no practical value. → Diogenes syndrome
explanation:
1) Diogenes syndrome (case 1) is characterized by hoarding of objects, usually of no practical use, and the neglect of one's home or the environment. It may present as a behavioural manifestation of various conditions including organic disorders, schizophrenia, depressive disorder, or obsessive-compulsive disorder, or refl ect a reaction late in life to stress in a certain type of personality. 2) Ekbom syndrome (case 2) is a monosymptomatic delusional disorder where the core delusion is a delusion of infestation. A conversion reaction with symptoms mimicking pregnancy with symptoms like nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and food cravings. It is sometimes seen in partners of expectant mothers during their pregnancy.

3) Somatising features of pregnancy is called Couvade syndrome (case 3). It is not delusional in nature, and the aff ected person does not believe they are pregnant (c.f. pseudocyesis). 4) Ganser symptom refers to the production of approximate answers as seen in case 4. Here the patient gives repeated wrong responses to questions, which are nonetheless approximately right. 5) Capgras syndrome is a type of delusional misidentifi cation. The patient believes that a person known to them has been replaced by a 'double' who is to all external appearances identical, but is not the real person.

stem: Adverse eff ects (1) Identify the type of side eff ects caused by antipsychotics, using descriptions given below. An 18-year-old gentleman commenced on haloperidol presents dramatically with eyes rolled upwards, and a twisted neck. 25-year-old woman on the ward commenced on risperidone is constantly pacing up and down, rocking from foot to foot and constantly crossing/uncrossing legs when seated. A 33-year-old gentleman was started on trifl uoperazine 5 days ago. He is now complaining of tremors, stiff ness and inability to initiate body movement. Choose... Choose... Choose...
correctAnswer: An 18-year-old gentleman commenced on haloperidol presents dramatically with eyes rolled upwards, and a twisted neck. → Acute dystonia, 25-year-old woman on the ward commenced on risperidone is constantly pacing up and down, rocking from foot to foot and constantly crossing/uncrossing legs when seated. → Akathisia, A 33-year-old gentleman was started on trifl uoperazine 5 days ago. He is now complaining of tremors, stiff ness and inability to initiate body movement. → Parkinsonism
explanation: Dystonias are brief or prolonged contractions of specifi c groups of muscles resulting in symptoms such as oculogyric crises, tongue protrusion, trismus, torticollis, blepharospasm. It is often seen in younger men receiving high dose of high-potency medications. Akathisia includes both subjective and objective - feelings and signs of restlessness. Patients may exhibit inability to relax, jitteriness, pacing, rocking with alternation of sitting and standing. Drug-induced parkinsonism is seen in 15-20% of patients treated with antipsychotics, seen within 90 days of treatment (5 to 90) and is characterized by muscle stiff ness, cogwheel rigidity, shuffl ing gait, stooped posture, and drooling.

Which one among the following is not a characteristic feature of Bion's basic assumptions?
explanation: The basic assumptions of Bion must be tackled to allow group work to proceed. Bion postulated that when people meet in a group basic assumptions become prominent. stem: Graded exercise therapy is a treatment option recommended for which psychiatric condition?
explanation: Graded exercise therapy is a treatment option recommended for Chronic fatigue syndrome. It is based physiological model of deconditioning. Muscles strength, autonomic response and perception of exercise related sensation are aff ected by inactivity. Therapy aims to increase gradually the exercise and other activities thus reducing the unwanted consequences of inactivity. CBT and graded exercise therapy are the only eff ective treatments for CFS.
